teen.text: Did you know that regular exercise, even just walking, can help reduce the severity of period cramps by releasing natural painkillers called endorphins?
Staying hydrated is super important! Drinking enough water can help reduce bloating, which sometimes makes cramps feel worse.

adult.text: Certain foods can influence period pain. For instance, foods rich in magnesium, like dark chocolate, nuts, and seeds, may help relax the uterine muscles and ease cramps.
For some people, reducing salt and caffeine intake a few days before their period is expected can help lessen bloating and discomfort associated with cramps.

teen.text: It's a cool fact that your body temperature naturally drops to help you fall asleep. A warm bath before bed can help kickstart that process, making it easier to drift off.
The blue light from screens (like phones and tablets) can trick your brain into thinking it's still daytime, making it harder to fall asleep. Try putting screens away an hour before bed.

adult.text: A consistent sleep schedule, even on weekends, is one of the most effective ways to improve sleep quality. It helps regulate your body's internal clock, or circadian rhythm.
While a glass of wine might make you feel sleepy initially, alcohol can disrupt your sleep cycle later in the night, leading to less restful sleep.

teen.text: Did you know that deep breathing is one of the fastest ways to lower stress? Taking a few slow, deep breaths sends a signal to your brain to calm down and relax.

adult.text: Chronic stress can sometimes deplete your body's magnesium levels. Including magnesium-rich foods like leafy greens, almonds, and avocados in your diet can be supportive.

teen.text: Quick reminder: the bodies you see on social media are often posed, filtered, and not a reflection of real life. Your body is unique and wonderful just as it is!
It's totally normal for your body to change a lot during your teen years. Try to focus on what your body can DO—like run, dance, or hug a friend—rather than just how it looks.

adult.text: Health looks different on every body. Instead of focusing on a number on the scale, try tracking things that really matter, like your energy levels, strength, and how you feel mentally.

teen.text: It's okay not to be okay! Having 'bad days' is a normal part of life. The important thing is to be kind to yourself and know that feelings come and go.
Talking about your feelings isn't a sign of weakness—it's a sign of strength. Sharing what's on your mind with a trusted friend, family member, or me can make a huge difference.

adult.text: Self-care isn't just bubble baths. It can be setting boundaries, saying 'no' to things that drain your energy, or taking five minutes of quiet time for yourself.
Did you know there are over a dozen types of contraception available? From daily pills to long-acting methods like IUDs, there's likely a method that fits your lifestyle perfectly.
Choosing a birth control method is a personal decision. It's always a great idea to chat with a healthcare provider to discuss the pros and cons of different options for you.
